what: Pressing a filter button makes the cards that no longer match fade in place while shrinking to .01x, the remaining cards slide to their new spots, and newly matching cards grow from small at their new spots. The list height shrinks or grows on the same beat so the content below doesn’t jump — all three move together over the same .6s (position and size eased, fade linear, MixItUp defaults), and removed cards leave the flow only once it ends
needs: CustomEase (to use curve values as they are)

options.dur: Duration (s), default .6 — 0 hides and shows immediately
options.ease: Curve (four numbers or GSAP name), default 0.25,0.1,0.25,1 (CSS ease)
options.scale: Scale when dropping out and coming in, default .01
options.[data-fx-part=filter]: Filter buttons — put the category name in data-f, leave empty for all. The active button gets is-on
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Card — list category names in data-cat separated by spaces for multiple
options.fade: Blur curve, default 0,0,1,1 (linear) — measured against the original, only position and size use ease
options.delay: Delay (seconds) before the motion starts after a click, default 0 — the original (MixItUp) starts a frame or two late while measuring a list of over 70 cards

note: The original is MixItUp 3 (commercial license), so it is not used. The same behavior (fade scale, 600ms, ease, list height fit) is rewritten from scratch. It measures start, middle (a layout that still keeps cards about to leave in the flow) and end positions, and changes only the offset values over the middle layout. GSAP Flip absolute mode makes every card jump at once at the end, so it is not used. With many cards (over 70), low-end devices shorten dur.
